1

the short version

  • Mistral never reads the PDF → reads a picture of each page
  • picture ≈ 1,024 px on the long side. any page size. always.
  • letter page → text 13–15 px → near-perfect
  • our long emails = 5–18× a letter page → same 1,024 px → text 2–4 px
  • no OCR reads that → empty / garbage / invented text
  • not in Mistral docs. not in Azure docs.
  • found in Oct, from the picture size Mistral sends back per page
so…
· not our bug
· retry / repair / prompt can't fix it → detail gone before reading
· predictable: page shape + font size
· 24 of 55 files have an unreadable page, 15 more unreliable
· since 9 Oct → bad pages skip Mistral → LlamaParse

worst case: Mistral 0% · LlamaParse 97% of the text ✓

what we built, one symptom at a time

4 Sep
broken-output detection · re-OCR via SDK · AI repair agent (LangGraph)
re-OCR = same tiny picture again. repair agent also sees a picture (≤ 2,048 px) → 8,096 pt email = 0.25 px/pt → 8 pt text = 2 px for it too
5 Sep
guards: don't reuse a bad OCR result
stops reuse. output still bad
23 Sep
"advance OCR" → every page through the repair agent
same limit as the repair agent
28 Sep
LlamaParse fallback when output looks broken
works · only after Mistral + re-OCR + repair ran (and were paid for) · only if damage is detected
9 Oct
root cause found → unreadable pages go straight to LlamaParse
~1,650 lines of OCR code in Sept.
each one → a symptom.
none → the cause. cause unknown.

that's where a big chunk of September went.

3

the photocopier

  • copier that always prints on the same small card · ~1,024 dots, long edge
  • letter page on the glass → fits → every word sharp
  • 2-metre email printout → shrunk to the same card → each line a thin grey smear
  • Mistral = that copier. reads the card, never the original
only two things matter:
① longest side of the page
② font size
taller page ≠ more pixels.
same pixels, spread thinner.

4

the maths

text px = font pt × ⌊ 73,728 ÷ long side pt ⌋ ÷ 72

73,728 = 1,024 × 72  ·  72 pt = 1 inch

UPLIZNA eCRM Email 4 · p2 (the 28-char page)
page601 × 3,987 pt · 8.3 × 55 in
dpi1,024 × 72 ÷ 3,987 = 18.49 → 18
picture151 × 997 px · Mistral reported exactly this
text14 pt × 18 ÷ 72 = 3.5 px
needs~8 px or more
0% returned
JASCAYD 152055 · p3 (plain US letter)
page612 × 792 pt
dpi1,024 × 72 ÷ 792 = 93.1 → 93
picture791 × 1,023 px
text10 pt × 93 ÷ 72 = 12.9 px
needs~8 px or more
100% returned

how sure?

  • every page Mistral returns → carries its picture size + dpi (dimensions)
  • 67 pages · 14 files · incl. every example here
  • rule → exact dpi, every time · picture size within 1 px
  • long side always lands between 997 – 1,024 px
5

what Mistral actually gets

  • each picture rendered at exactly the dpi Mistral used → same pixels it got
  • left: those pixels, enlarged, one square each · nothing added
  • right: same part of the page, at a size people can read
  • Mistral's renderer may smooth edges a bit differently · pixel count (the limit) is the same
left strip = everything Mistral had.

7

why product should care

smallest print goes first

ISI + boxed warnings → often the smallest font on the page → first text lost → exactly what ISI validation + claim checks need

fails silently

no error · "success" response · just less text, garbage, or made-up words · without a check → asset looks processed

retries = money, no gain

every extra pass → the same shrunken picture

10

limits

  • font size = a proxy · from the PDF text layer · text inside images has no font size · big headings lift the median → hence the small-print column
  • 5 px / 8 px bands ← 67 measured pages, mostly readable · clear at the extremes · 5–8 px genuinely mixed
  • 4,096-token output limit (Azure card) → real, but not a hard per-page cut in our data (one page came back ~5,900 tokens) · picture size explains the failures · token cap may add on very dense pages
  • Mistral can change its rendering any time → the per-page dimensions will show it
